summary: Across a 500-tree Random Forest and a permutation-importance analysis on a held-out test set, 'capital-gain' is the single most important predictor of income class (mean ROC-AUC drop of 0.0486 when permuted), followed by relationship, education-num, age. RF Gini importance cross-checks this closely (capital-gain and relationship are its top two). A logistic-regression cross-check's raw coefficient ranking is dominated by native-country/occupation, but that is an artifact of summing many sparse one-hot coefficients for high-cardinality columns rather than genuine importance -- those same features rank lowest under permutation importance, so capital-gain, relationship/marital-status, education, and age remain the most credible top predictors overall.
primary_metric_name: top feature permutation importance (mean ROC-AUC drop)
methodological_choices: Target binarized as class=='>50K'. '?' tokens treated as missing and encoded as a distinct category. 70/30 stratified train/test split, random_state=42. Primary model: RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=500, min_samples_leaf=2) with ordinal-encoded categoricals (unknown/missing given sentinel codes), unweighted despite ~76/24 class split since ROC-AUC is threshold-independent. Feature importance measured primarily via permutation importance (mean decrease in test-set ROC-AUC over 10 shuffles per feature) rather than RF impurity-based (Gini) importance, since Gini importance is biased toward high-cardinality/continuous features (e.g. fnlwgt, capital-gain) and can be misleading; permutation importance was computed on held-out data. Random Forest Gini importances and a logistic regression (one-hot encoded, standardized numerics, |coefficient| summed per original feature) are reported as cross-checks; note the LR |coefficient|-sum ranking is inflated for high-cardinality categoricals (native-country, occupation) since summing many sparse one-hot coefficients is not a fair comparison against single continuous features, so it is treated as a weaker signal than permutation importance. fnlwgt (census sampling weight) was kept as a feature but flagged as not a genuine demographic predictor. RF test ROC-AUC: 0.9165, accuracy: 0.8656; Logistic Regression test ROC-AUC: 0.9069.
